scope: Independent read-only review of four final runtime source bindings, exact 12-sample root Shader review consumption, and before-await progress persistence in the existing budget/lifecycle harnesses. No browser, game generation, final108 runtime run, binder proposal, or ledger mutation.

findings.topic: Four reports and four source audits
findings.conclusion: buildProposal reads production/equivalence/budget/lifecycle by their exact receipts, invokes numeric/report validation for all four, then requires four distinct report paths and exactly one matching source binding per kind. Each binding must concern the same final source and report bytes, exit0 and exact before/after served hashes. Missing, duplicate, wrong-kind, wrong-source and wrong-report evidence cannot fill a missing method.

findings.topic: Independent Shader review is not inferred from numeric success
findings.conclusion: A separate SHA-bound receipt must name root, bounded-independent-shader-pass, the exact finalSource/lifecycle/sourceBinding, a nonempty ownership conclusion and limitations, and all 12 actual label/created/live/active tuples in order. Technical evidence also binds this same receipt. The numeric validator pending-separate-receipt result alone cannot satisfy this gate.

The package-index emitter iterates the compiled native catalogue without sorting the index. Binder IDs therefore retain the same order required by the numeric lifecycle mixed world/grade/seed schedule; the later set comparison does not replace this ordered runtime check.

The recorded receipt hashes match the reviewed current binder/check/qualification plan and contains exactly 40 passed predicates. Its four-binding cases use explicitly synthetic metadata, while Shader count tuples use the original real52 lifecycle report. Missing reports/audits, duplicate audits, wrong report bytes and missing/wrong root/source/report/audit/Shader counts are rejected. This is not a full final108 proposal baseline.

The exact world/severe/20261004 identity is written before context creation and any case await. New successful-case writes occur after the original sample and screenshot; no new filesystem write enters the 12 held-key measurement intervals. Catch records the same current identity and failure while retaining prior cases. Fixed inputs, durations, counters, thresholds and lack of retry are unchanged.

findings.topic: Lifecycle progress persistence preserves reconstruction and GC sequence
findings.conclusion: Initial load, six warmups, baseline, ten identical builds, each mixed identity and the final return are recorded before their first await. Sampling is recorded before the original two GC calls, and completed samples/coverage survive catch. Seed arithmetic, catalogue order, selection, 500ms settle, two 50ms GC waits, resource assertions and no-retry strategy are unchanged.

limits: The final108 actual reports and full real-evidence baseline/negative proposal remain pending; this review grants neither runtime nor iteration qualification.

Numeric runtime validator implementation was authored by this reviewer. Its independent ownership review is root evidence linked above; this receipt independently reviews pipeline binder/check and progress patches, rather than self-signing the numerical implementation.

Progress persistence was reviewed from the narrow source diff and producer syntax receipt, not tested with a new browser fault. Budget progress is case-level; lifecycle records reconstruction and sampling phases. Browser launch/setup failures before a case begins remain process/wrapper failures rather than invented world identities.

Operator-declared exclusiveWindow is not proof of exclusive scheduling. Final budget/lifecycle execution must still exclude other Chrome/heavy CPU work; no GPU driver byte/RSS claim or artwork/play-experience approval is made.
Human/root identity is an explicit repository review receipt in this local workflow, not a cryptographic authentication mechanism. The binder cannot itself perform that independent judgment.
